newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybean losses push soyoil to fresh lows.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybean losses push soyoil to fresh lows.

text.p: Sharp losses in CBOT soybean futures helped push all nearby soyoil months to more contract lows Wednesday.
Soymeal futures were also lower, under pressure from weak cash markets and spillover weakness from soybeans, traders said.
"The meal and bean basis has gotten a lot softer this week," said one analyst.
Rail basis offers for soymeal in Illinois markets were down $1.00 per ton in response to growing supplies at processors and weak demand, cash dealers said.
U.S. export sources said that soyoil prices here were still too dear for most foreign buyers. Purchases are not likely until prices fall further, they said.

In early soymeal trade, Cargill bought 100 lots August and Refco and Smith Barney each sold 100 lots July, pit traders said. In soyoil trade, Cargill bought 300 lots July, 100 August and 100 December.
At 1138 CDT, July soymeal was $3.20 per ton lower at $269.70, and other months were $0.50 to $2.70 lower. July soyoil was 0.10 lower at 22.62 cents a lb, and other contracts were 0.05 to 0.13 lower.
